book_title: Chapter 8. Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup
question: Does TXN's November 20, 2026 chart confirm Stage 2 support or a Stage 4 institutional breakdown across daily, weekly, and 4-hour timeframes?

epigraph.quote: When a market leader breaks both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages on double normal volume during a 10-distribution-day downtrend, capital preservation overrides bottom-fishing.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein & William O'Neil Synthesis

web_blocks.html: Texas Instruments' technical picture deteriorated sharply between November 13 and November 20, 2026. On November 20, TXN plunged -7.70% in a single session (from $285.75 to $263.75) on 16.82M shares—1.99x its 20-day average in the facts ledger (1.95x TradingView's 30-day average; 2.49x Finviz's average).[12][13][15] Weekly losses reached -13.13% in the facts/Finviz ledger (-15.41% over TradingView's 1-week window), leaving TXN -21.04% below its $334.03 52-week high.[12][13][15] Crucially, Friday's break sliced beneath every major daily and weekly support: 50D SMA ($286.38, -7.90%), 30W SMA ($285.65, -7.67%), 10W EMA ($281.84, -6.42%), S1 pivot ($277.54), 200D SMA ($266.37, -0.98%), and 40W EMA ($264.22).[13]

Transparent Stage Split Disclosure (Facts Stage 1 vs. Snapshot STAGE_4): Readers should note an exact classification split across our two technical ledgers. The quantitative facts_US_2026-11-20.json screen labels TXN Stage 1 (Basing) because its 50-day SMA ($286.38) is still mathematically higher than 21 sessions ago ($272.18) and close sits -0.98% near the 200D SMA, even while recording 7 distribution days over 25 sessions.[15] By contrast, snapshots_US_2026-11-20.json assigns STAGE_4 (AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN, ceiling CAP_REJECTED) because price sits -7.67% below the 30-week SMA ($285.65) and -7.90% below the 50-day SMA ($286.38) with a TradingView moving-average rating of -0.93 (Strong Sell).[13] We follow the stricter STAGE_4 discipline: broken 50D, 30W, and 200D averages on 2x volume forbid new entries.

Multi-Timeframe 1W / 1D / 4H Alignment & Options Desk Readout: All three chart horizons point downward with zero reversal signal. On the Weekly (1W) chart, RSI stands at 47.34 with price below both the 10W EMA ($281.84) and 30W SMA ($285.65).[13] On the Daily (1D) chart, RSI fell to 36.12, 14-day ATR expanded to $14.07 (5.33% of CMP), Bollinger Band width widened to 20.01%, and Friday's 20-day swing low hit $262.29—just $0.29 above our prior $262.00 stop.[13][15][16] On the 4-Hour (4H) chart verified in options_US_batch4.json, 4H RSI is oversold at 29.16 far below 4H EMA20 ($290.83) and 4H SMA50 ($295.07), with intraday_4h_turn: false.[16] The Options Desk assigns NO_OPTIONS_EDGE ('No clean call-spread strikes available above $215 on 2027-02-19; stand aside'), confirming no tactical bounce trade exists.[16]

web_blocks.title: Tape Rule: Respect the 200-Day Break and Exit Ahead of a Gap Through $262.00
paragraphs: Our prior $262.00 stop was designed to exit if TXN lost its 200D SMA and 40W EMA. Both broke on November 20 on ~2x volume, leaving a $1.75 buffer against a $14.07 daily ATR. Exiting now at $263.75 avoids waiting for a Monday gap toward $248–$254.

book_paragraphs: Between November 13 and November 20, 2026, the technical evidence on Texas Instruments flipped from constructive Stage 2 digestion to decisive Stage 4 breakdown. On Friday, November 20, TXN dropped 7.70% in a single day from $285.75 to $263.75 on 16.82 million shares—1.99 times its 20-day average volume in the market-facts ledger, 1.95 times TradingView's 30-day average, and 2.49 times Finviz's normal volume. That capped a brutal 13.13% weekly slide (-15.41% on TradingView's 1-week window) and pushed shares 21.04% below their $334.03 52-week high.

Just as important as the magnitude of the drop is what broke underneath it. Friday's close at $263.75 pushed TXN decisively below every major institutional trendline: the 50-day SMA at $286.38 (-7.90%), the 30-week SMA at $285.65 (-7.67%), the 10-week EMA at $281.84 (-6.42%), the S1 pivot at $277.54, the 200-day SMA at $266.37 (-0.98%), and the 40-week EMA at $264.22. With daily ATR expanding to $14.07 (5.33% of share price), Friday's intraday swing low of $262.29 came within 29 cents of our prior $262.00 structural stop.

We also disclose a subtle technical split between our two automated ledgers. Because the 50-day SMA ($286.38) remains mathematically above its level 21 trading days ago ($272.18), the mechanical facts ledger still tags TXN as Stage 1 (Basing) despite seven distribution days over the past 25 sessions. Meanwhile, the live snapshot evaluator classifies TXN as STAGE_4 (AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN, gate CAP_REJECTED) because price sits nearly 8% beneath both the 50-day and 30-week averages, reinforced by a TradingView moving-average rating of -0.93 (Strong Sell). Institutional risk management requires honoring the stricter STAGE_4 ceiling.

Multi-timeframe alignment confirms there is no edge in catching this falling knife. On the weekly chart, 14-week RSI sits at 47.34 below falling near-term averages. On the daily chart, 14-day RSI has dropped to 36.12 with Bollinger Band width expanding to 20.01%. On the 4-hour chart captured in our options snapshot, 4H RSI sits deeply oversold at 29.16 far below its 4H EMA20 ($290.83) and 4H SMA50 ($295.07), with intraday_4h_turn marked false. Consequently, our Options Desk outputs NO_OPTIONS_EDGE—there are no clean call spreads and no confirmed mean-reversion turn.

book_subsections.title: Market Downtrend, Semiconductor Breadth Collapse & Stop Breach Logic
paragraphs: The macro tape amplifies every single-stock crack. As of November 20, 2026, the U.S. equity market has transitioned into a full Downtrend: only 38.8% of tracked stocks hold above their 50-day moving averages, 46.9% hold above their 200-day averages, and the major indices have logged 10 distribution days over the past 25 sessions. Only one of eleven market sectors remains above its 20-day moving average.

Semiconductors have lost their leadership cushion right alongside the market. TheWrap's sector ranking dropped Semiconductors from #12 on November 13 to #21 on November 20, as industry breadth plunged to just 17.0% above 50-day EMAs and 26.0% above 200-day EMAs. Every single tracked analog peer—Analog Devices ($345.92), NXP Semiconductors ($235.15), Microchip ($55.44), and ON Semiconductor ($60.84)—is now flagged in STAGE_4. Short interest in TXN remains low at 2.01% of float (2.72 days to cover), proving that Friday's 16.82 million share selloff came from institutional de-risking rather than speculative shorting.

Look at what that means for our prior $262.00 stop-loss. When we set $262.00 on November 13, it sat intentionally beneath the 200-day SMA ($264.77) and 40-week EMA ($264.24) to act as our structural Stage 2 boundary. Today, TXN closed at $263.75—already below the 200-day SMA ($266.37) and 40-week EMA ($264.22)—leaving just $1.75 (0.66%, or 0.12x daily ATR) before $262.00 triggers. Waiting for a 66-basis-point tick lower inside a 10-distribution-day Downtrend invites a weekend gap down toward the S2 pivot ($254.25) or 63-day base low ($248.13). Exiting cleanly now respects the true spirit of our stop rule.

book_callouts.title: Why 0.12 ATRs Is Not a Buffer
book_callouts.text: With ATR14 at $14.07 and TXN already beneath its 200D SMA ($266.37) and 40W EMA ($264.22), holding for the last $1.75 down to $262.00 exposes the position to gap risk toward $248–$254.
